papers.evidence: 从无位姿图像学习场景几何并预测相机，与Transformer三维重建主题直接相关
papers.tldr: 论文重新审视自监督三维几何学习中的非对称设计：传统方法在输入空间隔离上下文视图与待预测视图，虽能提升渲染，却可能牺牲深度和相机估计。作者改在三维表示空间排除待重建视图，同时让共享骨干利用全部视图建立对应关系，并借助稀疏—稠密视图特征对齐及冻结视觉基础模型增强几何信号。实验显示，该方案无需几何标注即可改善深度与位姿估计，优于既有自监督方法，并能提升后续监督训练。
papers.abstract_en: Self-supervised learning relies on asymmetry between what a model observes and what it must explain. Recent methods learn 3D geometry from unposed images by predicting cameras and scene structure, then rendering held-out views. To avoid trivial solutions, they impose this asymmetry in the input space, restricting how views interact through separate branches or masked attention. We revisit this design with geometric accuracy, rather than rendering quality, as the main objective. When a held-out view lies between context views, the context already constrains the geometry it observes. We therefore impose the asymmetry in the 3D representation space, excluding held-out views only from the reconstructed scene while a shared backbone uses all views for correspondence. This improves depth and pose estimation over input-space designs. We further exploit view density: sparse and dense observations depict the same scene but provide different amounts of correspondence. Aligning sparse-context features with dense-context features supplies a geometric training signal alongside rendering, without a pretrained geometric teacher. We additionally align features with a frozen vision foundation model, which brings further gains. None of these signals requires geometric annotation, and the resulting model improves geometry estimation over prior self-supervised methods. Controlled experiments isolate the contribution of each component, and self-supervised pretraining also improves subsequent supervised training.

papers.title_en: Scaling Trusted Autonomy: Towards Generally Capable Verifiable Robots
papers.authors: Benedict Quartey
papers.evidence: 结合学习策略与符号规划，提升机器人自主性和行动可验证性
papers.tldr: 基础模型让机器人具备开放语言理解、陌生物体识别和跨环境操作能力，但仍难以证明其真正理解指令、动作会产生预期效果，或内部状态符合现实。本文提出以神经符号方法扩展可信自主性，结合可学习模型的泛化能力与符号规划、验证结构。通过LIMP、REALM和PACTS分别处理指令落地、场景状态更新与技能组合恢复，推动构建可检查、可重规划的通用机器人。
papers.abstract_en: Robots powered by foundation models are increasingly able to interpret open-ended language, recognize unfamiliar objects, and operate across diverse environments. Yet broader capability does not establish that a robot has understood a request, that its actions will produce the intended effects, or that its internal representation still corresponds to reality. Classical symbolic planning provides explicit structure for composition and verification, but traditionally depends on hand-engineered skills and representations. Learned policies can broaden the robot's repertoire, but provide weak guarantees about what will happen and why. This thesis argues that scaling trusted autonomy requires a neurosymbolic approach that unifies the generality of learned models with symbolic structure for robust robot behavior. It explores three complementary directions. First, LIMP uses foundation models and spatial reasoning to ground natural-language instructions in explicit task constraints and instruction-specific semantic maps, enabling task-and-motion planning while exposing the robot's interpretation for inspection. Second, REALM maintains an editable, photorealistic 3D Gaussian scene, predicts the consequences of planned manipulation, and locally reconciles the scene so that subsequent instructions obtain their grounding and planning geometry from an updated state. Third, PACTS learns visuomotor skills that jointly generate action trajectories and predictions of their symbolic effects, supporting skill composition, progress monitoring, and recovery through replanning. Together, these contributions preserve explicit structure for reasoning and verification while broadening how it is obtained, providing a foundation for generally capable robots whose behavior can be assessed under the assumptions of their models.

papers.title_en: Align3D: Image-Structure Co-Aligned 3D Scene Generation with Observability-Aware Fidelity-Preserving Guidance
papers.authors: Chenliang Zhou, Yifan Wang, Andrzej Banburski-Fahey
papers.evidence: 结合置信度场景图的三维室内场景建模
papers.tldr: 单张室内照片难以同时恢复与观测一致、且在视野外仍物理合理的三维布局，现有方法常在图像保真与场景质量间失衡。Align3D从图像推断带置信度的场景图，并以图像—结构协同对齐训练集合扩散布局去噪器。进一步通过可观测性感知的保真引导，让低观测区域吸收物理先验而不破坏已对齐信息。在3D-FRONT上同时提升图像对齐和场景质量，且推理时单次前馈即可处理未见照片，兼顾生成质量与实用效率。
papers.abstract_en: We present Align3D, an image-conditioned diffusion model that generates 3D indoor layouts that are both faithful to a single input photograph and physically plausible beyond the observed view. From the photograph we infer a confidence-calibrated scene graph and train a set-diffusion layout denoiser with image-structure co-alignment where confidence-weighted modality fusion balances image and scene-graph alignment using predicted confidences, while observability-aware fidelity-preserving guidance projects conflicting scene-quality gradients and reweighs them with an object-level confidence mask so under-observed degrees of freedom absorb physical priors without undoing the image-graph match. On 3D-FRONT, Align3D improves image-alignment and scene-quality metrics over recent baselines; once trained, it maps previously unseen photographs to layouts in a single feed-forward pass.

papers.title_en: Segmenting Geometric Textures of 3D Meshes
papers.authors: Weidan Xiong, Kaijie Qu, Shihao Feng, Shunqi Fan, Rongyu Xiong, Hui Huang
papers.evidence: 面向三维网格中层几何纹理的分割
papers.tldr: 现有三维网格分割多聚焦于高层语义部件，难以识别具有装饰性和结构性的中层几何纹理，视觉语言模型也存在三维纹理理解不足的问题。本文构建几何纹理分割基准并针对性微调SAM3，利用DINO特征相似度聚类二维纹理区域，再将结果提升到三维网格。实验表明，该方法显著优于现有方法，并支持模型编辑、纹理相似检索等应用，为文化遗产保护、三维打印和网格处理提供实用工具。
papers.abstract_en: Recognizing geometric texture patterns on 3D models is critical for applications such as heritage protection, model editing, and 3D printing. Existing 3D model segmentation methods predominantly focus on identifying high-level semantic parts, thereby failing to capture middle-level textures. While recent Vision-Language Models can perform image segmentation with appropriate text prompts, they still struggle to recognize 3D geometric textures. In this work, we present a method that segments 3D mesh models based on middle-level geometric textures. We further introduce a new geometric texture segmentation benchmark and fine-tune SAM3 accordingly. The segmented texture regions are then clustered based on DINO feature similarity and lifted from 2D to 3D. Additionally, we develop an interactive tool to enable both 3D model editing based on our segmentation results and model retrieval from the dataset based on geometric and texture similarity. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing methods in segmenting geometric textures and can facilitate various applications.

papers.title_en: RadarDINO: Distilling a Visual Foundation Model into mmWave Radar for Human Mesh Reconstruction
papers.authors: Furkan Mert Algan, Zhifan Ni, Eckehard Steinbach
papers.evidence: 利用蒸馏视觉语义进行雷达人体网格重建
papers.tldr: 毫米波雷达具备隐私友好和不依赖光照的优势，但高保真人体网格重建仍受点云稀疏、漏检及原始雷达张量语义不足等问题限制。RadarDINO将视觉基础模型DINOv3的语义蒸馏至三维雷达表示，并结合标定的RGB-雷达几何关系提供体素级与身体部位级监督，同时加入顶点和关节几何损失。在M4Human数据集三个评测划分上均超越现有最佳基线，提升了雷达表示的细粒度建模与人体重建能力。
papers.abstract_en: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers a privacy-preserving and illumination-robust alternative for human mesh reconstruction (HMR). However, high-fidelity radar HMR remains challenging. Sparse point cloud-based methods suffer from information loss and missed detections, while raw radar tensor methods like RT-Mesh lack fine-grained semantics and explicit local body modeling. In this paper, we propose RadarDINO, a radar HMR framework that distills visual semantics from a DINOv3 teacher into 3D radar representations and introduces explicit geometric supervision. DINOv3 descriptors are transferred to radar voxels via calibrated RGB-radar geometry, providing voxel- and body-part-level supervision for part-aware radar representations. We further incorporate vertex- and joint-losses to directly constrain reconstructed geometry. On the M4Human dataset, our method outperforms the SOTA baseline across all three evaluation splits.

papers.title_en: Video Stitching from Multiple Moving Cameras
papers.authors: Shira Ifergane, Roy Amoyal, Shahar Benishay, Oren Freifeld
papers.evidence: 采用空间变换器网络进行多视角几何对齐
papers.tldr: 针对多台自由移动相机拍摄同一场景时难以进行几何对齐、现有方法又多局限于双相机或固定视角关系的问题，论文提出MViS轻量级测试时优化框架。方法通过时空变换器风格网络，在短时间窗口内联合处理所有视角并预测逐视角、逐时刻单应性，再以几何引导对齐和外观细化两阶段优化保证多视角与时间一致性。实验表明，MViS在双视角基准上达到或超过现有最佳方法，并发布多相机自由运动视频数据集与首个对应基准，推动复杂场景下的视频拼接研究。
papers.abstract_en: We address geometric video alignment for the same scene captured by multiple freely moving cameras. Existing methods, which are based on image stitching or video stabilization, are typically limited to two cameras or must assume the restrictive setting of a fixed linear ordering of the cameras. We propose MViS, a lightweight test-time optimization framework for joint multi-view alignment with temporal consistency. MViS uses a spatial-transformer-inspired net to jointly process frames from all views within a short temporal window and predict per-view, per-time homographies. Optimization proceeds in two stages: geometry-guided alignment followed by appearance-based refinement, with both stages enforcing multi-view and temporal consistency across the sequence. The method requires no scene-specific hyperparameter tuning, handles arbitrary and time-varying view-intersection graphs, and remains robust under rapid camera motion. On a standard two-view video benchmark, MViS matches or surpasses the state of the art. To facilitate evaluation in more complex scenarios, we introduce an annotated dataset with more than two freely moving cameras and establish the first benchmark for this setting. Project page: https://bgu-cs-vil.github.io/MViS-project/ .

papers.title_en: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video
papers.authors: Fan Zhu, Rui Yu
papers.evidence: 利用度量鸟瞰场景记忆理解视频环境
papers.tldr: 视频中的三维空间推理受限于视角局部、缺乏持续度量场景记录，固定RGB帧还可能遗漏稀疏或遮挡线索。BEV3SR将带相机参数的RGB-D视频构建为可查询的度量鸟瞰场景记忆，并按证据需求分流几何计算与视觉对齐。仅用16帧预算即能稳定提升多种视觉语言模型在多项三维场景问答基准上的表现，尤其改善空间密集型与开放式问题。该免训练、骨干无关且可解释的框架实现了高效显式的三维推理。
papers.abstract_en: 3D spatial reasoning from video remains challenging for VLMs because videos provide sequential, view-local observations rather than persistent metric scene records. Many questions must be answered in a query-specified perspective rather than the observed camera viewpoint, and prompting with a fixed set of RGB views may miss sparse or occluded visual cues. To address these gaps, we introduce BEV3SR, a training-free and backbone-agnostic framework for RGB-D videos with camera parameters. BEV3SR turns video observations into queryable metric bird's-eye-view (BEV) scene memory and formalizes each query into an evidence-aware spatial task. The Spatial Task Formalizer specifies the query's reference frame, spatial constraints, objective, and evidence requirement. The evidence requirement determines the appropriate reasoning pathway. A query treated as requiring geometric evidence is handled by the Geometric Reasoner, which deterministically computes the answer using the metric BEV records in the query-specified reference frame. Otherwise, a query treated as requiring visual evidence is passed to the Visual Evidence Aligner, which uses BEV-indexed object records and their associated supporting views to retrieve object-consistent and scene-context RGB frames for VLM grounding. Within a standard 16-frame budget, BEV3SR consistently improves different VLM backbones across multiple 3D scene QA benchmarks, delivering large gains on spatially intensive questions and significant improvements on open-ended scene QA. These results demonstrate that BEV3SR offers an effective, efficient, and interpretable framework for explicit 3D spatial reasoning from video.

papers.title_en: eSharp: Diffusion-based Sharp Monocular Metric Event-to-Depth Estimation
papers.authors: Qiushi Dai, Aniket Dashpute, Yuhao Liu, Rishubh Parihar, Guha Balakrishnan, Ashok Veeraraghavan
papers.evidence: 面向快速运动和高动态范围场景的单目度量深度估计
papers.tldr: 针对传统单目深度估计在快速运动和高动态范围场景中易失效、事件数据又缺乏稠密深度标注的问题，论文提出事件相机深度估计框架eSharp。该方法复用预训练扩散模型先验，并通过跨模态蒸馏利用与事件相机空间配准的帧相机生成经激光雷达校准的稠密伪标签。实验表明，eSharp在真实数据上同时提升了度量深度精度与空间锐度，优于已有事件到深度方法。研究证明扩散模型可为事件驱动的三维感知提供有效基础。
papers.abstract_en: Depth perception is fundamental for autonomous navigation, industrial inspection, and mixed-reality systems. It often operates under strict constraints on power and form factor. In such cases, monocular depth estimation (MDE) is often used. Even as recent advances continue to improve monocular depth quality, conventional frame-based MDE systems remain challenged by fast motion and high-dynamic-range scenes. This work introduces eSharp, an MDE framework that addresses these problems using an event camera. eSharp repurposes pretrained diffusion priors for event-only MDE and produces accurate metric depth with unparalleled sharpness on real data. Real-world event datasets provide only sparse LiDAR depth maps for ground-truth supervision, making dense prediction challenging. We address this limitation through cross-modal distillation, using LiDAR-calibrated dense pseudo-labels generated from a spatially co-registered frame camera to train eSharp. Experiments show that eSharp outperforms prior event-to-depth baselines in both metric-depth accuracy and spatial fidelity, establishing diffusion models as a promising foundation for event-driven 3D perception.

papers.title_en: MetricPose: Flexible 3D Human Pose Estimation with Depth and Geometric Cues
papers.authors: Shifan Zhu, Sabad Modi, Hang Yang, Arushi Agrawal, Steven Gao, Meghan Huber, Nathan Wycoff, Donghyun Kim
papers.evidence: 结合深度、相机位置与环境约束的三维几何估计
papers.tldr: 单目三维人体姿态估计不仅要恢复关节构型，还要确定人体尺度及其相对相机的真实位置，但透视投影使人体大小与相机距离存在内在歧义。MetricPose在预训练全身姿态估计器上引入可选的度量深度与环境几何模块，融合RGB先验、深度测量和地面接触等约束，并以共享参数支持RGB、RGB-Ground与RGB-D。相较SAM 3D Body，三种模式的相机局部关节位置误差分别降低12.16%、31.00%和54.61%。该方法在保持纯RGB能力的同时，实现了更灵活、尺度准确且具环境感知的三维定位。
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we present a 3D human pose estimator that predicts metrically accurate human joint positions in the camera coordinate frame. This task requires recovering the configuration of the body joints, scale, and metric camera-local placement. In monocular images, body size and camera distance are coupled through perspective projection and therefore cannot be determined uniquely from image alone. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining three complementary sources of information: learned RGB priors, direct depth measurements, and geometric constraints (e.g., ground contact) from the environment. We extend a pretrained full-body estimator with optional metric depth and geometry-processing modules that improve camera-distance estimation and depth-guided body refinement while preserving RGB-only operation. The resulting unified model supports RGB, RGB-Ground, and RGB-D using shared learned parameters. Unlike pelvis-relative error, camera-local error also measures placement relative to the camera. Compared with the existing foundation model SAM 3D Body, our methods with RGB, RGB-Ground, and RGB-D modes reduce camera-local joint-position error by 12.16%, 31.00% and 54.61% respectively.

papers.title_en: ExQuery: Explicit Structured Query Priors for Temporal 3D Object Detection
papers.authors: Honglin Sun, Yifei Zhang, Junyang Zhang, Kenji Hashimoto
papers.evidence: 显式组织三维检测中的几何与运动状态查询
papers.tldr: 时序三维目标检测中的稀疏查询，往往把语义、几何与运动信息混合编码，削弱了物理状态的结构性。ExQuery将查询拆分为共享语义上下文及中心、尺寸、朝向、速度等状态切片，并贯穿先验编码、分支回归和时序重建。模型结合自车运动变换、分类软语义先验与门控仿射调制，融合历史实例特征。在nuScenes上取得有竞争力的检测性能，消融实验验证各模块有效，说明显式结构化先验有助于提升时序检测建模能力。
papers.abstract_en: Sparse query-based 3D detectors commonly encode heterogeneous semantic, geometric, and motion information into unified latent queries, including when explicit 3D anchors are used. We introduce ExQuery, an explicit structured query framework for temporal 3D object detection. Each decoded query is organized into a shared semantic context slice and physical-state-specific slices for center, dimensions, orientation, and velocity. This structure is preserved from prior encoding to branch-specific regression and is reused to reconstruct temporal queries: predicted physical states are transformed by ego motion, classification scores form soft semantic priors, and the reconstructed query is fused with the stored latent instance feature through gated affine modulation. Experiments on the nuScenes benchmark show that our method achieves competitive detection performance, and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our proposed modules.

papers.title_en: DAC-MACE: Context-Conditioned Expert Routing for Compact Scene Coordinate Regression in Camera Relocalization
papers.authors: Dingying Fan, Mingkai Liu, Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Xianliang Huang, Qian Zhang, Xueqian Wang, Fei Qiao
papers.evidence: 通过上下文场景坐标回归改进相机位姿估计
papers.tldr: 相机重定位需要在紧凑场景地图中从图像恢复绝对位姿，但现有基于混合专家的场景坐标回归依赖局部描述子路由，易混淆不同位置的重复立面与窗户。DAC-MACE通过残差上下文适配器、全局上下文编码器和图像级描述子改进软路由，并结合双阈值RANSAC—LM位姿估计。在剑桥地标数据集上平均中位平移误差达13.0厘米，优于GLACE和MACE；还在7-Scenes提升召回率。该方法增强了大规模户外场景的辨识与定位能力。
papers.abstract_en: A camera becomes an absolute pose sensor when its images can be relocalized against a prebuilt map of the scene. On mobile robots and augmented-reality devices, that map must be small and quick to build. Scene coordinate regression (SCR) stores the scene in a compact network that predicts a 3D coordinate for every pixel, and mixture-of-experts (MoE) variants extend its capacity to larger outdoor scenes. In existing MoE-based SCR, however, the router assigns each pixel to an expert from the same local descriptor that the experts regress from, so repeated facades and windows at different locations receive similar routing inputs. We present DAC-MACE, which conditions soft expert routing on recalibrated and contextualized features. A residual context adapter (RCA) reweights the channels and locations of frozen encoder features, a global context encoder (GCE) mixes them with multi-scale self-attention, and an image-level pooled descriptor is added to the router input. A dual-threshold RANSAC--Levenberg--Marquardt estimator recovers the pose. On Cambridge Landmarks, DAC-MACE attains a mean per-scene median translation error of 13.0 cm over three seeds, the lowest among the RGB-only SCR methods compared (GLACE 13.6 cm, MACE 14.4 cm), and reduces the error on the largest scene from 24 to 19 cm relative to MACE. In a cumulative study, the MoE head, GCE, RCA, and the dual-threshold estimator lower the mean error from 17.0 cm to 14.4, 14.0, 13.6, and 13.0 cm. On 7-Scenes, adding GCE to a single ACE head raises Recall@(5 cm, 5$^\circ$) from 86.56% to 87.60%.

papers.title_en: MambaLoc: Lightweight Indoor Localization Using Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation
papers.authors: Mohab Bahnassy, Omar Saqr, Hamada Rizk, Moustafa Youssef
papers.evidence: 支持边缘设备机器人导航的轻量室内定位
papers.tldr: 室内边缘设备上的高精度定位面临模型能力与计算开销的矛盾。Wi-Fi CSI成本低却受多径干扰，Transformer效果较好但难以实时运行，UWB精确却需要专用基础设施。MambaLoc以线性复杂度的Mamba作为CSI学生模型，并借助UWB-Transformer教师模型进行跨模态知识蒸馏，再结合特征对齐与高斯混合回归刻画空间歧义。真实数据表明其中位误差达0.230米，较独立Mamba降低22.2%，同时显著减少计算量与延迟，实现无需UWB硬件的高效定位。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate indoor localization on resource-constrained edge devices remains challenging due to the tension between modeling fidelity and computational efficiency. Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) enables low-cost deployment using existing Wi-Fi infrastructure but is heavily distorted by multipath propagation. Transformer-based solutions mitigate these effects but their quadratic complexity limits real-time edge deployment. Ultra-Wideband (UWB) provides geometrically precise ranging yet requires dedicated infrastructure. We present MambaLoc, a cross-modal distillation framework that improves the accuracy-efficiency balance in CSI-based localization. MambaLoc uses a linear-time Selective State Space Model (Mamba) as a lightweight CSI student, guided during training by a UWB-Transformer teacher. A Feature Alignment Module bridges the representational gap between heterogeneous RF modalities, allowing the CSI model to inherit UWB-derived geometric structure without UWB hardware at inference. A probabilistic Gaussian Mixture regression head models multi-modal spatial ambiguity from multipath effects, avoiding the physically implausible averaging of deterministic regression. Evaluations on a real-world dataset show MambaLoc achieves a median localization error of 0.230 m, reducing error by 22.2% over a standalone Mamba baseline, while requiring 65.1% fewer FLOPs and 58% lower inference latency than Transformer-based approaches.
